# Playbook for Hf_Kuhn_Nerfed

## Declaration Strategy

When I reach showdown, I will declare the card I actually hold. My opponent has announced they will declare truthfully once then lie optimally afterward. Declaring honestly maintains my own credibility and prevents me from being predictably exploited. The opponent's strategy of declaring first gives them an information advantage; I should not compound this by also bluffing unpredictably.

## Betting with Strong Hands

When I hold a King, I will bet when I open the action, regardless of chip position. The King is the strongest hand and wins showdowns. Building the pot with my strongest holdings is fundamental to positive expectation.

When I hold a King and my opponent checks to me, I will bet. This extracts value from weaker holdings.

## Betting with Medium Hands

When I hold a Queen and open the action, I will bet. The Queen beats Jack and loses only to King. Opening with aggression when I have a reasonable hand establishes pressure and takes the initiative.

When I hold a Queen and my opponent checks to me, I will bet. Checking has not recovered my chip deficit; betting with moderate hands when given the initiative is more profitable.

## Betting with Weak Hands

When I hold a Jack and open the action, I will check, not bet. The Jack is the weakest hand and wins only against nothing. Betting with Jack from the button has not been profitable in my record.

When I hold a Jack and my opponent checks to me, I will check as well. Checking keeps the pot small when I am behind in hand strength.

## Against the Declared Liar

My opponent's declaration gives them a structural advantage. I cannot overcome this through clever play; I can only minimize losses by playing sound poker fundamentals: value betting my strong hands, checking my weak hands, and declaring honestly at showdown.
